Class analysis: this is the FOURTH instance of one failure mode, and the per-instance fix is not the fix.

Prior instances, all the same test (`test_no_new_torch_before_dotenv_vm_entrypoints`), all found the same way —
someone else's Step 9c gate going red on a script they never touched:

- #933 — stale #895 grandfather entry (same file)
- #2314 — `scripts/issue2225_fu2_dod_points_fig.py`
- #2487 — `scripts/issue823_shared_persona_paired.py` (landed by `d526008c67`; filed 2026-08-23, still `proposed`)
- #2550 (this task) — `scripts/issue2254_firstk_ctxext_sensitivity.py` (landed by `fd8222d6f7`)

**Why it keeps recurring — and it is the same structural defect #2537 is open on.**
`tests/test_shared_vm_thread_caps.py` is a WHOLESALE SCANNER: `_scan_targets` walks the `scripts/**/*.py`
class, so it is a genuine consumer of EVERY script entrypoint in the repo. But the Step 9c selector maps a
changed file to tests by stem match, name-derived glob, and explicit registry entries — all NAME-based. A
session adding `scripts/issue<K>_<whatever>.py` therefore gets no mapping to this test, the test never runs at
that session's landing gate, the script lands green, and the test goes red on `main` for everyone afterward.
Each subsequent session then pays reviewer and orchestrator turns proving the red is foreign (four such probes
on #2537 alone: the Claude reviewer, the Codex twin, the implementer, and the orchestrator).

This is #2537's own bug class one step further out. #2537 closes "consumer tests named after the FEATURE rather
than the module", where a name-based rule *could* have matched but did not. A directory-class scanner is the
harder case: no name-based rule could EVER connect `scripts/issue2254_*.py` to
`tests/test_shared_vm_thread_caps.py`, because the dependency is on the file's DIRECTORY MEMBERSHIP, not its
name. And #2537's own new discovery meta-test does not cover it either — that meta-test looks for
constructed-path loader calls (`spec_from_file_location` and local wrappers), not directory scanners.

**Candidate structural fix (proposal only — NOT adopted here, and deliberately NOT folded into #2537).**
Make scanner-consumers run whenever their scanned class changes. Two shapes worth pricing:

1. Register `tests/test_shared_vm_thread_caps.py` (and any sibling that scans a whole directory class) as a
   `WORKFLOW_INVARIANT` member, so it runs at every gate regardless of the diff. Cost: its measured wall is
   ~95 s standalone at moderate load, which is over 3x #2537's entire 30 s budget for one invariant file — so
   this is probably too expensive as-is and would need the scan narrowed to the diff's own paths first.
2. Add a selector rule mapping any ADDED-or-MODIFIED `scripts/**/*.py` path to the scanner tests that consume
   that class — a directory-membership arm alongside the existing stem/glob/registry arms. Cheaper at gate
   time (it fires only when the class actually changes) and it generalizes to other scanner tests.

Shape (2) looks right, and it is a selector change, so it is adjacent to #2537's file. It is NOT being folded
into #2537: that task is mid-review-ensemble with a plan whose acceptance criteria and deviation bounds are
already fixed, and adding a new selector arm now would be exactly the planner-introduced-scope anti-pattern its
own round-1 critique warned about. It wants its own task with its own cost analysis — particularly the
gate-wall question, since a directory-membership arm fires on a very common diff shape.

**Immediate scope of THIS task is unchanged**: the two-line ordering fix for
`scripts/issue2254_firstk_ctxext_sensitivity.py`. The class analysis is recorded here so a fifth instance
routes to the structural fix instead of filing a fifth one-line repair.

**Fleet context.** At filing time the infra dispatch cap (5) was full and at least four of the open siblings are
trunk-red tasks of this same general family (#2549 shared-tmp-name red, #2528 stale ledger misclassifying
main-side reds, #2487 above, #2414 ungated upload call site). The backlog is the symptom; the selector's
blindness to non-name-based consumers is a large part of the cause.
